// Part: room: wing balcony walk. The walk is a 1-wide strip x49..57 on z62 (y11..16 air), entered from the wing opening
// at z61 x52..53 and open at its west end onto the living room's balcony edge (the rail at x48 y11 belongs to the shell).
// Nothing stands on the floor, because every floor cell is the walk. Light hangs from two iron_chain + lantern pairs under
// the ceiling, placed off the doorway cells, so the strip reads lit from end to end.
import { B } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";

export function build(g) {
  // lanterns hang from the ceiling (y17) on a chain: chain y15..16, lantern y14 (hanging) over the walk
  for (const x of [50, 56]) {
    g.set(x, 16, 62, ...B.chain("y"));
    g.set(x, 15, 62, ...B.chain("y"));
    g.set(x, 14, 62, ...B.lantern(true));
  }
}

Roof off-palette warnings in make.sh output (tuff_brick_slab, tuff_bricks, cobbled_deepslate_stairs, polished_deepslate_slab, and others) come from roof.json, not this part. They were not touched.

waste.what: Working out which cells were locked. I had to probe the whole walk box by writing 54 lanterns, rebuilding, and restoring the file, to learn that every walk cell was refused and not just the two columns.

waste.what: Trying move candidates (x=50/56 to x=51/55) by hand, with a full rebuild for each guess, before checking whether the box was claimed at all.
waste.tool: The same free-cell query would have answered it before any guess: a box of cells with no earlier-part claim, or the answer 'none' for this whole room.
